explanation: Baseline feedback recorded two distinct failure kinds within the learning scope of the supplied tasks: `object_type` at action 0 for most tasks and `resource_limit` (sandbox_execution_failed) for two tasks. The most likely shared cause of `object_type` is the strict tuple-based normalization (`tuple(f)` on lists works, but `men.add(...)` typing heuristics and `_typed` silently dropping malformed entries leave type sets wrong), plus the `("carrying", ...)` indexing in the old code; the resource_limit is consistent with unbounded full-state BFS over a large branching factor. This revision: (1) normalizes every atom via `_norm_atom` so list-style JSON input is handled uniformly, and string forms; (2) derives man/spanner/nut/location sets from both the type table and the observed predicates without the previous no-op fallbacks; (3) replaces the full-state BFS with a targeted constructive search (BFS only over the location graph for walking paths), bounding plan length to MAX_STEPS=1000 so no plan can exceed the required bound. Observations are drawn only from the recorded baseline for this task family.
